title: 1973 AHSME Problem 28
statement: If \(a,\) \(b,\) and \(c\) are in geometric progression (G.P.) with \(1\lt a\lt b\lt c\) and \(n\gt1\) is an integer, then \(\log_a n,\) \(\log_b n,\) \(\log_c n\) form a sequence

answerChoices.label: C
answerChoices.text:
in which the reciprocals of the terms form an
A.P.

answerChoices.label: D
answerChoices.text:
in which the second and third terms are the \(n\)th powers of
the first and second respectively

solutions.text:
By change of base, \[ \begin{aligned} \frac1{\log_a n}&=\log_n a,\\ \frac1{\log_b n}&=\log_n b,\\ \frac1{\log_c n}&=\log_n c. \end{aligned} \] Since \(a,\) \(b,\) \(c\) are in geometric progression, \(b^2=ac.\) Taking logarithms to base \(n\) gives \[ 2\log_n b=\log_n a+\log_n c. \] Hence the reciprocals of the three given terms form an arithmetic progression.

Therefore, the correct answer is C.
hints: Take reciprocals and use \(\dfrac1{\log_a n}=\log_n a\)
Apply logarithms to the geometric-progression relation \(b^2=ac\)
